title: The Rs 9 Lakh Gesture: When Salman Khan Took a Loan to Buy His Father a Rolex
excerpt: Bhai's story about buying Salim Khan a luxury watch on borrowed money is peak desi family drama — and every NRI child who's ever overspent on their parents felt it
body:
When Salman Khan tells a story about his father, you stop scrolling. On a recent podcast appearance that's now making the rounds across every Bollywood fan page on the planet, Bhai revealed that early in his career — long before the Being Human empire, the farmhouse parties, and the Rs 2,000-crore net worth — he once took out a loan to buy his father Salim Khan a Rolex watch worth Rs 9 lakh.

The Watch That Started an Argument

The elder Khan's reaction was not what you'd expect from a man receiving a luxury timepiece. "Do you consider yourself a king?" Salim Khan reportedly asked his son, bewildered by what he saw as reckless extravagance from a young actor who didn't yet have the bank balance to justify a Rolex purchase.

It's the kind of story that resonates deeply in desi households — the complicated dance between wanting to shower your parents with gifts and the older generation's instinctive discomfort with what they perceive as wasteful spending. Every NRI who's ever tried to buy their parents a business-class ticket home knows this exact conversation.

From Disapproval to Daily Wear

But here's the twist that makes the story quintessentially Bollywood: Salim Khan eventually came around. The legendary screenwriter — one half of the Salim-Javed duo that gave Hindi cinema Sholay, Deewar, and Don — reportedly became so attached to the watch that it became part of his daily uniform. The gift that was initially dismissed as royal delusion became a cherished possession.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DYaJnvXqrSQ/

Salman also used the moment to debunk persistent rumours about his watch collection. Despite being photographed wearing what appeared to be a Rs 20-crore Patek Philippe at the Ambani pre-wedding celebrations, Khan insists he owns just one Rolex. "Most of my watches are gifts from friends," he said — a statement that somehow makes a man worth thousands of crores sound almost modest.

The Jacob & Co. Connection

The watch story gains another layer when you consider Salman's recent collaboration with luxury watchmaker Jacob & Co. on "The World Is Yours" dual time-zone collection — a limited-edition line inspired, in part, by his father's watch and designed for global travellers. It's the kind of full-circle moment that Salim Khan himself might have written into a screenplay.

Why This Story Hits Different for the Diaspora

For the millions of Indians abroad who grew up watching their parents wear the same Rs 500 Titan for decades while quietly funding their children's dreams, the Rolex story is less about luxury and more about a universal immigrant-family truth: the first generation sacrifices, the second generation wants to give back, and the negotiation between those impulses is where the real drama lives.

Salman Khan may be many things — polarising, unpredictable, endlessly meme-able — but when he talks about his father, he sounds like every desi kid who ever wanted to say "you gave me everything, let me give you something back." The Rs 9 lakh Rolex was never about the watch. It was about the gesture.

And if Salim Khan is reading this somewhere, still wearing that Rolex: the son did good, sir.
